manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the green orange and place it in the bowl.

Task description: The target is the green orange below and to the right of the light-blue bowl near the center of the table. Place it inside the bowl.

Success criteria: The green orange is stable in the light-blue bowl and supported by it; the gripper is open and no longer holding the fruit.

## Execution tips

- Use the finger pads to grasp opposite sides of the orange around its wider middle section. Set the opening slightly wider than that section, and confirm the fingers enclose the fruit before closing to avoid catching only the top or pushing it to roll.
- Test-lift slightly to see whether the orange slips relative to the pads. If it needs another grasp, let it rest on the table for support before releasing, avoiding a drop while suspended.
- When carrying the orange toward the bowl mouth, leave height clearance for its bottom and both fingers to cross the rim. Make larger pose adjustments in open space outside the bowl to reduce sweeping rim collisions.
- Release the orange away from the bowl rim and leave room for the fingers to open. Consider releasing only after the orange is supported inside the bowl, to avoid it bouncing out from a height or the gripper spreading against the bowl wall.

The green orange and light-blue bowl positions are confirmed. During pose adjustment, the controller reported a recoverable joint-limit rejection and the arm stopped at a new measured pose. I will adjust the approach from that state without repeating the rejected target.

The arm has approached the target gradually from above, and neither the orange nor bowl has visibly moved. Next I will align with the orange's middle and descend in small steps to confirm the fingers enclose the fruit before closing.
The target is between the spread fingers, but the gripper is still above the fruit. Descend in steps of no more than 1 cm, checking the contact position and table clearance at each step.

The orange remains supported by the table and has not visibly rolled. The gripper is approaching both sides of the fruit; after closing, I will make a small test lift and move it to the bowl only if it does not slip.
The gripper has closed to about 45.9 mm, and the view shows both pads contacting the fruit. I will first test-lift it by 1 cm to check whether the orange rises with the gripper.
The orange moved relative to the pads during the test lift, so a stable grasp is not confirmed. I will lower it back to table support before adjusting the grasp depth and closure amount.

After the adjustment, the orange rose with the gripper, and its position relative to the pads remained nearly stable during two consecutive test lifts. Next I will lift it high enough to clear the bowl rim, then move it laterally to the center of the bowl opening.
The orange is suspended securely above the bowl opening and has not been released. I will adjust it to the center of the bowl in small steps and lower gradually, leaving room for the fingers to open.

The current view shows the fruit above the central area inside the bowl, and the grip remains stable; the bowl has not moved. I am descending by centimeters and checking the gap between the fruit bottom and bowl interior.
The fruit is within the bowl opening, with no visible rim collision or bowl movement. Next I will approach the bowl's support surface using smaller steps, release, and observe stability.

The gripper is open, with a measured opening of approximately 64.4 mm. The image shows the orange remains inside and supported by the bowl. I will raise the gripper slightly, confirm full separation and fruit stability, then end this episode.
